_comment: Candidate rows for node arxiv-1902.10565::cfg_9x9_override, written by the worker and NOT appended. An independent validator refutes or admits them. Append order: result row first (python3 phys-agentic-loop/_common/result_database.py append), then the knowledge row (python3 phys-agentic-loop/_common/knowledge_database.py append), both from the az root with CHANDRA_ROLE set. Both carry a verification.command that the gate EXECUTES at append; the knowledge row's is the expensive closing check and needs a Slurm allocation.

candidate_result_row.name: 9x9-only selfplay and gatekeeper configs plus the 9-board train wrapper, key-diffed against upstream and proven by an executed selfplay run

working_context.cluster: skipjack, partition b200, 1x NVIDIA B200, --cpus-per-task=24, --mem=64G, slurm job 298359 on gb205
working_context.board: 9x9 only: bSizes = 9, bSizeRelProbs = 1, allowRectangleProb = 0, dataBoardLen = 9, trainer board length 9
working_context.net_under_test: none exported; the models dir is empty, so LoadModel::findLatestModel returns modelFile /dev/null (loadmodel.cpp:77-93) and setup.cpp:126 makes it a random-play net (debugSkipNeuralNet). No GPU work is performed; the allocation exists so that the thread measurement has a declared CPU count to compare against
working_context.cpu_policy: no CPU cap (human decision 2026-09-03, mission.json decisions[0], compute.cpuCapPerJob = null); the surviving rule is that --cpus-per-task must be declared honestly and not exceeded

candidate_result_row.claim: The mission-owned codes/cfg/selfplay_9x9.cfg, codes/cfg/gatekeeper_9x9.cfg and codes/loop/train_9x9.sh differ from the upstream *_maxsize9 presets and from python/selfplay/train.sh only in the board-size, row-size and thread keys (OUT_OF_SET_KEYS = 0 and 0; one changed line in the train wrapper); the selfplay config makes katago selfplay produce exclusively SZ[9] games (37 of 37 sgf lines, 0 rectangular); the train wrapper carries the board length 9 exactly once and 19 zero times; and the live selfplay process peaks at 22 OS threads against the 24 CPUs the job declared. Claims c04_9x9_only_games, c05_pos_len_9_pipeline and the selfplay clause of c06_threads_le_24.

verifier_result.command: sbatch /scratch/schmidt/ssci-anima/ssci-haiyangw/ktg-train/runtime/cfgcheck/cfg_9x9_check.sbatch  (job 298359), which runs: bash results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/eval/check_cfg_9x9.sh && test $(grep -c -- '-pos-len 9' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/loop/train_9x9.sh) -eq 1 && grep -q '^numGameThreads = 18' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/cfg/gatekeeper_9x9.cfg
verifier_result.output: CHECK_CFG_9X9: PASS; OUT_OF_SET_KEYS(1_selfplay) = 0; OUT_OF_SET_KEYS(2_gatekeeper) = 0; n_all = 37; n9 = 37; SZ9_FRACTION = 1.000; n_rectangular = 0; NLWP_MAX = 22 over 52 samples vs CPU_BUDGET = 24; grep -c '-pos-len 9' train_9x9.sh = 1; grep -c '-pos-len 19' train_9x9.sh = 0; numGameThreads = 18 in both configs

verification.command: grep -q 'CHECK_CFG_9X9: PASS' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/cfg_9x9/check_cfg_9x9-298359.txt && grep -q '^OUT_OF_SET_KEYS(1_selfplay) = 0' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/cfg_9x9/check_cfg_9x9-298359.txt && grep -q '^OUT_OF_SET_KEYS(2_gatekeeper) = 0' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/cfg_9x9/check_cfg_9x9-298359.txt && grep -q '^SZ9_FRACTION = 1.000' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/cfg_9x9/check_cfg_9x9-298359.txt && test $(grep -c -- '-pos-len 9' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/loop/train_9x9.sh) -eq 1 && test $(grep -c -- '-pos-len 19' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/loop/train_9x9.sh) -eq 0 && grep -q '^numGameThreads = 18' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/cfg/gatekeeper_9x9.cfg && grep -q '^numGameThreads = 18' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/cfg/selfplay_9x9.cfg && grep -q '^dataBoardLen = 9' results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/codes/cfg/selfplay_9x9.cfg

assumptions: a05_9x9_only: the mission trains on 9x9 only; upstream ships no 9-only preset and the mirror is read-only, so the configs must be mission-owned copies.

a10_random_bootstrap_ok: an empty models dir is not an error. The parse run therefore exercises the config, the game initializer, the data writer and the SGF writer, but not the CUDA backend - nneval.cpp:134 skips the compute context when debugSkipNeuralNet is set.

The SZ[9] proof is over 37 sgf lines from two short runs (1 game and 36 games), not over a production cycle. It certifies that the sampler cannot emit another size (bSizes has one entry, allowRectangleProb = 0), not that a long run stays 9x9 for some statistical reason.
The thread measurement covers katago selfplay only. The gatekeeper, shuffle and train rows of the DESIGN.md thread table remain arithmetic until their own nodes measure them.
The comparison threshold is the CPUs this job declared (24), not a policy cap - the 20 % clause was withdrawn by the human on 2026-09-03 (mission.json decisions[0]).
candidate_result_row.provenance: worker, task cfg_9x9_override, slurm job 298359; candidate row written to results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/cfg_9x9/candidate_rows.json for independent validation, not appended by the worker
open_obligations: o03_thread_budget_24cpu: the selfplay clause is measured here; the gatekeeper, shuffle and train clauses remain open until gatekeeper_stage / shuffle_stage / train_stage measure their processes.

o02_databoardlen_poslen_9: both halves are set in one commit, but the 'discard any pos_len-19 data before the first shuffle' half is vacuous only while no data exists; it becomes a live obligation for shuffle_stage.

visit-caps-9x9 and gate-visits-9x9 (convention.md section 10): maxVisits 600 / cheapSearchVisits 100 / gate 150 are carried over from 19x19 and are unchanged here; they close at selfplay_stage with a 9x9 games-per-hour derivation.
attn-logit (convention.md section 10): -attn-logit-penalty-cap is a train.py flag and is not set by this wrapper; it closes at export_stage.
candidate_result_row.notes: verification.command is the cheap evidence re-check, following the precedent of result row env-toolchain-b200; the expensive closing check that produced the evidence is in verifier_result.command and in the knowledge row's verification.command. Running the expensive one outside a Slurm allocation spawns 18 game threads on a login node capped at 14 cores and 5 GB - use srun -p b200 --gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=24 --mem=64G. The checker executes two selfplay runs: -max-games-total 1 (the spec'd parse proof) and -max-games-total 36 (2 games per game thread) for the ps -o nlwp sampling, because with one game total 17 of the 18 game threads break immediately at selfplay.cpp:291-293 and the peak would be a startup race. Check 4 counts SZ[9] over the sgf lines of both runs.

candidate_knowledge_row.summary: Mission-owned codes/cfg/selfplay_9x9.cfg, codes/cfg/gatekeeper_9x9.cfg and codes/loop/train_9x9.sh exist and are executed. Key-diff against cpp/configs/training/{selfplay1,gatekeeper1}_maxsize9.cfg touches only dataBoardLen 19->9, numGameThreads 128->18, bSizes 7,8,9->9, bSizeRelProbs 1,1,8->1, allowRectangleProb 0.50->0 (OUT_OF_SET_KEYS = 0 on both, significant line counts unchanged); the train wrapper differs from python/selfplay/train.sh in exactly one line (board length 9, count 1, and 19 count 0). katago selfplay with an empty models dir exits 0 and writes 37 sgf lines, 37 of them SZ[9] (fraction 1.000) with 0 rectangular; the live process peaks at 22 OS threads over 52 samples against the 24 CPUs the job declared. Slurm job 298359.
